requirements.requirement: Identify node1's interface facing lan-b and node3's counterpart interface
requirements.summary: Executor enumerated node1's interfaces (vtnet0/1/2) and node3's (enp1s0/enp8s0), then used ARP resolution to positively confirm L2 adjacency: node3's enp8s0 resolved a test IP assigned to node1's vtnet2 to a REACHABLE ARP entry whose MAC matched vtnet2's ether address, confirming vtnet2<->enp8s0 as the lan-b link.

requirements.requirement: Bring node1's lan-b interface into service as its own zone with an address on lan-b
requirements.summary: Added a new opt1/LANB interface bound to vtnet2 with static 10.100.47.1/24 and a firewall pass rule to config.xml, applied live via configctl interface reconfigure and filter reload; ifconfig confirms vtnet2 UP with the correct address and description 'LANB (opt1)'. Survived a full reboot with identical config observed post-restart.
node3's enp8s0 was configured persistently via nmcli to 10.100.47.3/24, and bidirectional ping to node1's 10.100.47.1 succeeded both before and after the full restart cycle of both nodes.

requirements.requirement: node3 reaches node2 on lan-a through node1's lan-b interface
requirements.summary: The executor demonstrated that node1 forwards traffic from lan-b (IP forwarding enabled, firewall pass rule present) by adding a temporary host route on node3 and observing a TTL decrement to 10.100.46.11 while it transited node1. However, 10.100.46.11 is node2's mgmt-network address (enp1s0, DHCP-assigned, same 10.100.46.0/24 subnet node3's own mgmt interface already sits on) — not an address on the lan-a network. Node2's actual lan-a-facing interface (enp8s0, per the topology's nic ordering) is shown throughout the trace with only a link-local IPv6 address and no IPv4 configured, and node1's own lan-a interface (vtnet1) was never given a persistent zone/address either. So the evidence proves node1 can route/forward lan-b traffic toward the mgmt network, but does not directly demonstrate node3 reaching node2 on the lan-a network specifically, because lan-a itself remains unaddressed on both node1 and node2 in every captured snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node1 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
requirements.summary: kern.boottime baseline captured pre-restart (1788626589), shutdown -r now issued, SSH timeouts observed during the transition, new kern.boottime confirmed post-restart (1788626912), and lan-b interface/address/reachability to node3 recovered.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node2 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
requirements.summary: boot_id baseline captured (fb2aa416...), systemctl reboot issued, connection errors observed during reboot, new boot_id confirmed (52851d02...), and connectivity to both node1 and node3 recovered post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node3 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
requirements.summary: boot_id baseline captured (d052eb57...), systemctl reboot issued, connection errors observed during reboot, new boot_id confirmed (35bee981...), and full recovery of enp8s0 addressing, routes, and reachability to node1 (lan-b) and node2's mgmt address.

overall_summary: The executor correctly identified node1's unconfigured lan-b-facing interface (vtnet2) and node3's counterpart (enp8s0) via ARP, brought vtnet2 into service as a new persistent OPNsense zone (opt1/LANB, 10.100.47.1/24) with a firewall pass rule, and configured node3's matching address (10.100.47.3/24), with node3<->node1 lan-b reachability verified both before and after a full restart of all three nodes. However, the claimed 'node3 reaches node2 on lan-a through node1' outcome is only partially substantiated: the destination pinged (10.100.46.11) is node2's mgmt-network address, not an address on the lan-a network, and node2's actual lan-a interface (enp8s0) is shown with no IPv4 address in every captured snapshot, as is node1's own lan-a interface (vtnet1). The restart evidence protocol was completed cleanly for all three nodes with clear boot-identity changes and recovered state. Hygiene is good overall, with only minor, low-risk, reverted troubleshooting mutations.
limitations: The 'reaches node2 on lan-a' requirement's supporting evidence targets node2's mgmt IP rather than a genuine lan-a address, and no evidence shows lan-a ever being addressed on node1 (vtnet1) or node2 (enp8s0) — this may reflect an environment/task-authoring gap (lan-a was never provisioned with addresses on either node) rather than an executor error, but it means the specific 'through it, on lan-a' claim lacks direct evidence.

Restart acknowledgements relied on backgrounded shutdown/reboot commands with polling; no kernel-level reboot log was inspected, though SSH timeout/reset patterns plus differing boot identities corroborate genuine reboots for all three nodes.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological trace: an initial identification approach (assigning temporary 169.254.9.x link-local test addresses to node1's vtnet1/vtnet2 and node3's enp8s0 via raw `ifconfig`/`ip addr`) failed repeatedly (cmd-70e08f0a190b4b6d, cmd-917dba3773ad4ec9, cmd-486fe637fe55440c, cmd-40471b6d46e341c7, cmd-de79ff3e1a7b4a14) before the executor switched to ARP-based confirmation and NetworkManager-persistent configuration; these were reasonable discovery attempts and were superseded by the final config (vtnet2 got a proper opt1/LANB persistent zone via config.xml, and node3's enp8s0 got a persistent nmcli profile), and the node1 reboot at the end reset any lingering ephemeral ifconfig state on non-persisted interfaces (vtnet1), so no residue remained. A config.xml backup (config.xml.bak) was created via shutil.copy before editing (cmd-8739dd4957174915) — a low-risk, standard safety practice, left in place but harmless. A temporary host route added on node3 to force traffic through node1 for the forwarding demonstration (cmd-997494be66b14c2e) was explicitly removed afterward (cmd-c5fdd384ea934d97), a bounded and fully reverted mutation. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed; failed-services and package-health snapshots are unchanged after_executor vs before_prepare for both CentOS nodes.
